messages:
nisha: Heads-up — customer Acme just escalated a batch rerank issue. They get 200 OK but scores seem assigned to the wrong queries (e.g., a high score for q2 shows up in q1 results). Also saw intermittent 403s earlier (token rotation) and a latency bump (~1.2s). Putting payload + logs below so we can triage quickly.

nisha: SAMPLE REQUEST (what customer sent)
```json
POST /v1/rerank/batch
Authorization: Bearer <token>
Content-Type: application/json

{
  "queries": [
    {"id": "q1", "text": "how to reset password"},
    {"id": "q2", "text": "company refund policy"}
  ],
  "candidates": [
    {"id":"c1","text":"reset steps"},
    {"id":"c2","text":"refund timeline"},
    {"id":"c3","text":"contact support"}
  ],
  "per_query_counts": [2,1]
}
```

nisha: Expected: candidates nested per query (e.g. "candidates_per_query": [[...],[...]]). Customer flattened to a single `candidates` array + per_query_counts. They claim this used to work but now top scores are misaligned.

support-bot: Created ticket TKT-4321 and attached original requestId and logs. Link: https://support.redwood.internal/TKT-4321 :white_check_mark:

sam: Can you paste the exact request_id and the server-side request/response logs? Also did the customer include any special headers (X-Customer-Project / x-api-client)? Need to repro locally. @oncall-ml can you triage if this looks like a batching offset bug? :eyes: 

nisha: request_id=req_20260315_9843, customer region us-west-2. Server log snippet (sanitized):
```
2026-03-15T14:12:03Z INFO  rerank-api req=req_20260315_9843 received batch size=2 per_query_counts=[2,1] candidates_len=3
2026-03-15T14:12:03Z WARN  reranker req=req_20260315_9843 candidate_map_method=flattened
2026-03-15T14:12:03Z ERROR reranker req=req_20260315_9843 candidate_index_offset bug: running_offset not reset per query shard -> assigned scores [0.95,0.40] to q1 but actually correspond to q2 candidate
```

nisha: Customer response payload (redacted):
```json
{
  "results": [
    {"query_id":"q1","scores": [0.95, 0.40]},
    {"query_id":"q2","scores": [0.88]}
  ]
}
```

eli: Looks like server treated the flattened list but the offset calculation is off when multiple shards/batch workers handle a request. Quick mitigation: validate that if `candidates` + `per_query_counts` are used, we compute offsets deterministically on the gateway and reject if inconsistent (400) with a helpful message. That would prevent customers from silently getting misaligned results.

eli: Proposed patch (small API-gateway schema check + unit test) and a runtime guard: https://git.internal/redwood/eng-runtime/pull/987 (draft). Also add a short kludge: if we detect total candidates==sum(per_query_counts) but per-query mapping doesn't match, log and return 400 instead of best-effort mapping.

sam: +1 to enforce strict schema. For now, please ask customer to switch to nested `candidates_per_query` or split into separate per-query rerank calls as a workaround. @oncall-ml please pick up the eng ticket and prioritize if this affects more customers.

nisha: Sent workaround + example to Acme. They will try nested payload this afternoon.

sam: Thanks. Also note the intermittent 403 — might be unrelated token rotation issue; I've opened infra-ops follow-up to check token expiry windows against the SDK. Filed INFRA-678.

nisha: Will update TKT-4321 when Acme confirms. Thanks everyone :pray:
